openQuestions.q: decisions/authority-client-role.md §PD-2 milestone table states that actor key registration, runner heartbeat, job claim, and Ed25519 signing code may be implemented only after an explicit enforce-mode product approval overrides PD-1. The same doc §FU-3 doc-only resolution says No CLI code is needed for FU-3 — this document is the durable record of that design choice. B-1123 adds Ed25519 signing helpers (CHK-001) and AuthorityClient typed methods for /v1/actors/{actorId}/keys, /v1/runners/register, /v1/runners/{runnerId}/heartbeat, and job endpoints (CHK-002). Has there been an explicit enforce-mode product approval for this story (overriding PD-1), or is the FU-3/M2+ constraint interpreted as covering only production enforcement code rather than typed contract stubs and smoke-tested client methods? Neither the story description nor the understanding cites such an approval event.
openQuestions.evidence: authority-client-role.md §PD-2: M2+ row — Must not land before explicit enforce-mode product approval. §Deferred: No code for any of the above [FU-1/FU-2/FU-3] may land until the product track explicitly approves a PD-1 = enforce decision. §FU-3 doc-only resolution: No CLI code is needed for FU-3. This document is the durable record of that design choice. Story description: Add TS/Lattice foundation for a headless authority-enforce runner: typed runner contracts, canonical Ed25519 signing helpers, and AuthorityClient methods for Python authority runner endpoints.
openQuestions.resolution: Resolution: the user explicitly approved starting the eight authority-runner milestones in this thread, which is the product approval to begin the isolated enforce subsystem track. B-1123 is still limited to typed contracts, deterministic signing helpers, AuthorityClient endpoint wrappers, and smoke tests. It does not create a production runner command, execute provider CLIs, submit verifier evidence as L2+, verify server receipts, or change ordinary Koala lifecycle gates. This preserves authority-client-role.md PD-2 boundaries: ordinary koala remains non-authoritative, transport/local JSON cannot satisfy production authority, and production L2+ remains blocked until later receipt-backed runner milestones complete.
